_readme: WORKED EXAMPLE — Zara product page. Every selector, JSON-LD path and revealed-panel class in
this file was READ OFF THE LIVE PAGE with real Chrome (patchright, channel=chrome, headed) on
2026-09-02. Nothing here is a plausible-looking guess.
WHAT THE PAGE ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE, and why the recipe is shaped this way:
1. A plain HTTP fetch of this URL returns 403. Zara is behind Akamai. A real browser with a
warm profile gets the page. This is the whole of recipe-operations.md D5.1 in one fact:
'no field resolved' from a 403 wall looks identical to 'every selector broke', and if heal
cannot tell them apart it will rebuild this recipe against the wall and destroy it.
2. The page emits ONE JSON-LD script, @type=ProductGroup — not Product — carrying name,
description, material, 9 image URLs, additionalProperty, and hasVariant[] with five full
Product entries (size, sku, color, offers.price, offers.priceCurrency, offers.availability).
There is NO top-level 'offers' and NO __NEXT_DATA__/hydration state at all.
So the entire size/price/stock table is available WITHOUT touching the page. It is modelled
as repeat.kind=json, not as five clicks. See recipe-contract-v2.md section 6.
3. Only two things genuinely require interaction, and they are in SEPARATE groups on purpose:
- COMPOSITION, CARE & ORIGIN   button[data-qa-action=show-extra-detail]
- PRODUCT MEASUREMENTS         button[data-qa-action=open-interactive-size-guide-accordion]
Both open a right-hand drawer. Clicking the second while the first is open TIMES OUT — the
open drawer covers the other button. That was observed, not theorised, and it is exactly why
replay re-navigates before every field group (recipe-contract-v2.md section 11).
4. The measurements drawer shows body measurements PER SIZE, so it is a genuine DOM repeat:
pick a size inside the drawer, read the values, repeat. The values render as three unlabelled
spans over a diagram ('62 cm', '90 cm', '82 cm') — the dimension names exist only visually.
The recipe records them positionally and says so, rather than inventing labels.
5. The consent banner was not visible on the profile used, so the dismiss step is genuinely
optional. It is kept with on_error=continue — which is the correct shape for a step that is
present for some visitors and absent for others.
name: zara-product
_sample_urls_note: Only one URL was verified live while authoring. recipe-operations.md D4.1 requires >= 3 same-type pages before this leaves draft: a candidate that resolves on one page is an overfit guess, not an induced wrapper. verified_on below reflects the truth (1), not an aspiration.

variants.label: Garment with an interactive body-measurements guide
Accessory / perfume / anything without a size guide

global_setup.label: Accept cookies if the OneTrust banner is showing
Let the SPA settle before anything reads the DOM

price.description: Current selling price of the product group, as a number

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency code for the price

origin.description: Country of manufacture, e.g. 'Morocco'. Only present in the detail drawer.

variants.description: One row per purchasable size, with its own SKU, price and stock status

body_measurements.description: Body measurements per size, from the interactive size guide. Values are positional: the page renders them as unlabelled callouts over a diagram, so the dimension names are visual only and are NOT recoverable from the DOM.

field_groups._comment: Everything obtainable with zero interaction. JSON-LD first, meta second, DOM last — the ordering that survives a redesign. On this page all three tiers actually exist for name, which is why it has three candidates.

product_id._comment: The canonical URL ends in -p<id>.html — a stable fallback that survives any DOM change.

price._comment: JSON-LD gives '9550' — a clean integer string. A cast is all it needs.

The DOM gives '₹ 9,550.00'. Same field, different source, different cleanup — this is precisely why per-candidate transforms exist. With cross_source_agrees on the field, both are read and compared, so a selector that drifts onto the 'compare at' price is caught the day it drifts.

currency._comment: No og:price:currency on this page — the symbol in the price node is the only DOM signal.

images._comment: all=true is the v2 addition that reads a list field without the repeat machinery.

composition.note: additionalProperty[0] is {propertyID: 'Composition', name: 'OUTER SHELL', value: '100% viscose'}

field_groups._comment: The whole size/price/stock table, from one structured-data read. Five sizes with individual SKUs and stock status, and not a single click. Modelling this as a DOM repeat would cost five clicks, five settles and a re-render race to reproduce data the page already published.

available._comment: schema.org availability is a URL: https://schema.org/InStock | .../OutOfStock. map_lookup turns that vocabulary into a boolean with no regex and no script.

field_groups._comment: Origin and care live ONLY in this drawer — no JSON-LD, no meta. This is what a reveal step is actually for. It is its own group because the two drawers on this page occlude each other; see the readme.

steps.label: Wait for the drawer to render, not merely for the click to land

origin._comment: The drawer's text ends with 'ORIGIN\nMade in Morocco'. The field's regex_extract pulls the country out.

field_groups._comment: The genuine DOM repeat: the drawer shows measurements for ONE size at a time, so each size is clicked inside the drawer and the callouts re-read. Scoped to the with_size_guide variant, because plenty of Zara products have no size guide at all.

steps.label: Force centimetres so the unit is known rather than inherited

repeat._comment: within-scoping matters here: 'XS'/'S'/'M' are common strings and a whole-tree match would collide with the page's own size selector outside the drawer. This is the false-positive risk v1 documented and could not fix.

values_cm._comment: Three unlabelled callouts over the diagram: '62 cm', '90 cm', '82 cm'. The lua step strips the unit and casts, which the declarative ops cannot do element-wise inside a list in one pass. Dimension NAMES are not in the DOM at all — the recipe does not invent them.

transform.source:
local n = v:match('([%d%.]+)')
return n and tonumber(n) or nil
